title: The Modern Cocktail on the Pantages vaudeville circuit
summary: He toured Pantages with a five-piece jazz act from Chicago to Seattle, sharing a bill with George Burns.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, yes, it had to go, say, six, about ten ways -- I'd make $5.00, $6.00 maybe a night, something like that, plus -- oh, yeah, I saved quite a bit, saved quite a bit as a youngster then. Then (while in unintelligible) Leroy's -- there was an act out on the road called The Modern Cocktail and [Pantages] it went into vaudeville then with this act on Plantageous circuit all the way to the coast and back. It was a jazz band, five-piece jazz band, singer and dancer.

No, no, vaudeville, vaudeville. If you -- you either did a full week or a split week. We called a split week -- three days in this town, four days in the other. There's no day off, you know, in vaudeville. If you worked a week in a theater you did seven days. So that was -- well, we did the Pantages, we picked it up in Chicago and went all the way out to Seattle and on down towards --
Did you travel with the whole show or --
No, no, just our pack. We were one time with the great Burns of Burns and Allen. He was the act ahead of
us when we did the lower circuit. He had a partner, he was a straight man and his partner was a comedian. George Burns. We traveled with him --
Yeah, yeah, George Burns. And one of those guys who did Tobacco Road -- we did the tour with him once.
